id: Practice Direction 70A – Enforcement Of Judgments And Orders

# PRACTICE DIRECTION 70A – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS

part70#id4541512

# This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89.] Contents of this Practice Direction

## SECTION I – GENERAL

## Definitions

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] A1.1 In this Practice Direction—

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (1) ‘writ of control’ is to be construed in accordance with section 62(4) of the Tribunals Courts and Enforcement Act 2007;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (2) ‘writ of execution’ includes-

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (a) a writ of possession;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (b) a writ of delivery;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (c) a writ of sequestration;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (d) a writ of fieri facias de bonis ecclesiasticis,

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] and any further writ in aid of any such writs, but does not include a writ of control.

## Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] 1.1 A judgment creditor may enforce a judgment or order for the payment of money by any of the following methods:

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] (1) a writ of control or warrant of control (see Parts 83 and 84);

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] (2) a third party debt order (see Part 72);

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] (3) a charging order, stop order or stop notice (see Part 73);

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] (4) in the County Court, an attachment of earnings order (see Part 89);

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] (5) the appointment of a receiver (see Part 69).

## 1.2 In addition the court may make the following orders against a judgment debtor –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 1.2 In addition the court may make the following orders against a judgment debtor –] (1) an order in contempt proceedings under Part 81, but only if the debtor is found in contempt of court; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 1.2 In addition the court may make the following orders against a judgment debtor –] (2) in the High Court, a writ of sequestration in an application under Part 83.

## 1.3 The enforcement of a judgment or order may be affected by –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 1.3 The enforcement of a judgment or order may be affected by –] (1) the enactments relating to insolvency; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 1.3 The enforcement of a judgment or order may be affected by –] (2) County Court administration orders.

## Proceedings for enforcement in the County Court – rule 70.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Proceedings for enforcement in the County Court – rule 70.3] 2.1 An application to enforce a judgment in the County Court may be made an any County Court hearing centre, unless an enactment, rule or practice direction provides otherwise.

## 2.2 Omitted

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 2.2 Omitted] 2.3 If for any reason proceedings for the enforcement of a judgment are transferred, the court will give notice of the transfer to all the parties.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 2.2 Omitted] 2.4 When the proceedings have been transferred, the parties must take any further steps in the proceedings in the court to which they have been transferred, unless a rule or practice direction provides otherwise.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 2.2 Omitted] (Part 52 and Practice Directions 52A and 52B provide to which court or judge an appeal against the judgment or order, or an application for permission to appeal, must be made.)

## Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3] 3.1 If a judgment creditor wishes to enforce a High Court judgment or order in the County Court, they must file the following documents in the County Court with the application notice or request for enforcement–

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3] (1) a copy of the judgment or order;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3] (2) a certificate verifying the amount due under the judgment or order;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3] (3) if a writ of execution or writ of control has previously been issued in the High Court to enforce the judgment or order, a copy of the relevant enforcement officer’s return to the writ; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3] (4) a copy of the order transferring the proceedings to the County Court.

## 3.2 In this paragraph and paragraph 7 –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 3.2 In this paragraph and paragraph 7 –] (1) ‘enforcement officer’ means an individual who is authorised to act as an enforcement officer under the Courts Act 2003; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 3.2 In this paragraph and paragraph 7 –] (2) ‘relevant enforcement officer’ means –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 3.2 In this paragraph and paragraph 7 –] (a) in relation to a writ of execution or writ of control which is directed to a single enforcement officer, that officer;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 3.2 In this paragraph and paragraph 7 –] (b) in relation to a writ of execution or writ of control which is directed to two or more enforcement officers, the officer to whom the writ is allocated.

## 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–] (a) be included in practice form N322B or, where paragraph 4.1A applies, in the practice form required by paragraph 4.1A(2);

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–] (b) specify the statutory provision under which enforcement or the recovery of a sum of money is sought;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–] (c) state the name and address of the person against whom enforcement or recovery is sought;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–] (d) where the decision or compromise requires that person to pay a sum of money, state the amount which remains unpaid; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–] (e) confirm that, where a sum of money is being recovered pursuant to a compromise, the compromise is not a conditional compromise.

## 4.1A

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (1) This paragraph applies where–

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (a) either –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (i) the decision to be enforced is a decision of an employment tribunal in England and Wales; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (ii) the application is for the recovery of a compromise sum under section 19A(3) of the Employment Tribunals Act 1996; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (b) the party seeking to enforce the decision wishes to enforce by way of a writ of control

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (2) The practice form which is to be used is–

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (a) where paragraph (1)(a)(i) applies, practice form N471;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (b) where paragraph (1)(a)(ii) applies, practice form N471A.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] 4.2 An application under rule 70.5(3) for an order to enforce a decision or compromise must be made by filing an application notice in practice form N322A.

## 4.3 The application notice must state –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.3 The application notice must state –] (a) the name and address of the person against whom the order is sought;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.3 The application notice must state –] (b) how much remains unpaid or what obligation remains to be performed; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.3 The application notice must state –] (c) where the application relates to a conditional compromise, details of what under the compromise the applicant is required to do and has done under the compromise in addition to discontinuing or not starting proceedings.

## 4.4 Where –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.4 Where –] (a) the application relates to a conditional compromise; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.4 Where –] (b) the application notice is served by the applicant on the respondent,

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.4 Where –] the applicant must file a certificate of service with the court within 7 days of service of the application notice.

## Registration of decisions in the High Court for enforcement – rule 70.5(8)

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Registration of decisions in the High Court for enforcement – rule 70.5(8)] 5.1 An application to the High Court under an enactment to register a decision for enforcement must be made in writing to the head clerk of the Action Department at the Royal Courts of Justice, Strand, London WC2A 2LL.

## 5.2 The application must –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 5.2 The application must –] (1) specify the statutory provision under which the application is made;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 5.2 The application must –] (2) state the name and address of the person against whom it is sought to enforce the decision;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 5.2 The application must –] (3) if the decision requires that person to pay a sum of money, state the amount which remains unpaid.

## Interest on judgment debts

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Interest on judgment debts] 6 If a judgment creditor is claiming interest on a judgment debt, he must include in his application or request to issue enforcement proceedings in relation to that judgment details of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Interest on judgment debts] (1) the amount of interest claimed and the sum on which it is claimed;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Interest on judgment debts] (2) the dates from and to which interest has accrued; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Interest on judgment debts] (3) the rate of interest which has been applied and, where more than one rate of interest has been applied, the relevant dates and rates.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Interest on judgment debts] (Interest may be claimed on High Court judgment debts under section 17 of the Judgments Act 1838. The County Courts (Interest on Judgment Debts) Order 1991 specifies when interest may be claimed on the County Court judgment debts.)

## Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] 6A.1 A judgment or order made against a partnership may be enforced against any property of the partnership within the jurisdiction.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] 6A.2 Subject to paragraph 6A.3, a judgment or order made against a partnership may be enforced against any person who is not a limited partner and who –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (1) acknowledged service of the claim form as a partner;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (2) having been served as a partner with the claim form, failed to acknowledge service of it;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (3) admitted in his statement of case that he is or was a partner at a material time; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (4) was found by the court to have been a partner at a material time.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] 6A.3 A judgment or order made against a partnership may not be enforced against a limited partner or a member of the partnership who was ordinarily resident outside the jurisdiction when the claim form was issued unless that partner or member–

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (1) acknowledged service of the claim form as a partner;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (2) was served within the jurisdiction with the claim form as a partner; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (3) was served out of the jurisdiction with the claim form, as a partner, with the permission of the court given under Section IV of Part 6.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] 6A.4 A judgment creditor wishing to enforce a judgment or order against a person in circumstances not set out in paragraphs 6A.2 or 6A.3 must apply to the court for permission to enforce the judgment or order.

## Payment of debt after issue of enforcement proceedings

## 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] (1) after the judgment creditor has issued any application or request to enforce it; but

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] (2) before –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] (a) any writ or warrant has been executed; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] (b) in any other case, the date fixed for the hearing of the application;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] the judgment creditor must, unless paragraph 7.2 applies, immediately notify the court in writing.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] 7.2 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid after the judgment creditor has applied to the High Court for a writ of execution or writ of control, paragraph 7.1 does not apply, and the judgment creditor must instead immediately notify the relevant enforcement officer in writing.

## SECTION II – ENFORCEMENT PROCEEDINGS IN THE CIVIL NATIONAL BUSINESS CENTRE

## Scope

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Scope] 8.1 This section applies to applications for orders to obtain information from judgment debtors and applications for enforcement of judgments made at the Civil National Business Centre where the proceedings have not been transferred or sent to a County Court hearing centre.

## Applications under Parts 71 and 72

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Applications under Parts 71 and 72] 9.1 Where an application is made to which rule 71.2(2)(b)(ii) or 72.3(1)(b)(ii) applies, it must be filed at the County Court hearing centre for the district in which the judgment debtor resides or carries on business.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Applications under Parts 71 and 72] Paragraphs 10.1 and 10.2 omitted.

## Transfer

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Transfer] 11.1 Unless the court is satisfied that the application does not comply with the Rules, it will transfer the proceedings to the hearing centre where the application was filed and a court officer will inform the Civil National Business Centre of the transfer.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Transfer] Updated: Thursday, 10 August 2023
